- Replaced `re.sub` sanitization + f-string in both ZIP download handlers with the same helper

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: marcusrbrown
body:
## Summary

Tooling cleanup in two commits:

1. **Remove JSON5 prettier-compat workaround** — `@bfra.me/eslint-config@0.50.3` ships the upstream fix, so the local override block in `eslint.config.ts` is no longer needed
2. **Pin Node 24 in CI** — fixes a latent CI gap exposed by transitive dep churn from the eslint-config bump

## JSON5 workaround removal

- Bump `@bfra.me/eslint-config` range from `^0.50.0` to `^0.50.3`
- Remove the scoped `**/*.json5` override block in `eslint.config.ts` (8 disabled rules + 4 lines of explanation comment)
- Update `bun.lock` (net -42 lines of transitive dep churn)

### Why

When `.github/renovate.json5` was moved back to JSON5 format in early April, two flat-config layers fought each other on that file:

- **`prettier/prettier`** wanted JSON5 style: unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing commas
- **`jsonc/quote-props`, `jsonc/quotes`, `jsonc/comma-dangle`** (and friends) wanted strict JSON: quoted keys, double quotes, no trailing commas

`@bfra.me/eslint-config` already had built-in handling for this — it would import `eslint-plugin-jsonc`'s `configs.prettier` compat config when the plugin was detected. Detection used `isPackageExists('eslint-plugin-jsonc')`, which returns `false` for transitive deps hidden inside Bun's `.bun/` symlink layout. So in Bun workspaces, the compat rules never loaded and the conflict surfaced.

### What landed upstream

[bfra-me/works#3047](https://github.com/bfra-me/works/pull/3047) (fixes [bfra-me/works#3045](https://github.com/bfra-me/works/issues/3045)) ships in `@bfra.me/eslint-config@0.50.3`. The preset now uses try/catch dynamic imports instead of `isPackageExists`, so it works regardless of the package manager's `node_modules` layout.

## CI Node pin

The second commit fixes a latent CI gap that the eslint-config bump exposed:

- `ci.yaml`'s lint and type-check jobs set up Bun only, with no `actions/setup-node`
- ubuntu-latest ships Node 20 on PATH by default
- `bun run lint` → spawns `eslint` binary via `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang, which resolves to the Node 20 on PATH
- `eslint-flat-config-utils@3.1.0` (new transitive dep pulled in by `@bfra.me/eslint-config@0.50.3`) calls `Object.groupBy`, an ES2024 API only available in Node 21+
- Node 20 throws `TypeError: Object.groupBy is not a function`

Fix: add `actions/setup-node@v6.3.0` with Node 24 to lint and type-check jobs, matching the Release workflow convention. The test job runs via `bun test --recursive` (Bun runtime, no shebang) and doesn't need the pin.

Without this pin, a local `bun run lint` (on machines with newer Node via mise/nvm/etc.) would pass while CI silently used whatever Node the runner image happened to ship with.

## Local verification

- `bun run lint` → 0 errors (only pre-existing `no-console` warnings on CLI/script files)
- `bun run fix` → no drift on `.github/renovate.json5` (upstream preset preserves the JSON5 style)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` → clean
- `bun test --recursive` → 104 pass

## Tracking

Closes the local tracking for [bfra-me/works#3045](https://github.com/bfra-me/works/issues/3045). The scoped override block is fully removed; no residual JSON5 overrides remain in `eslint.config.ts`.

Addresses Fro Bot review non-blocking concern about the changeset referencing the issue number instead of the fix PR — changeset body now references both.

author: zena-park
body:
## Summary

Security audit M-11: `lockingOrders` (in-memory Set) doesn't protect against race conditions when multiple relayer instances run in parallel.

### Problem

```
Instance A: onRemoteOrderArrived() → lockingOrders.add(orderKey) → sendTradeOffer()
Instance B: onRemoteOrderArrived() → lockingOrders.add(orderKey) → sendTradeOffer()
                                     ↑ different Set, doesn't see A's lock
```

Both instances match the same order → double-settlement attempt (on-chain nullifier catches it, but wastes gas).

### Fix

DB-level optimistic lock before matching:

```typescript
// Check DB status (shared across instances)
const dbOrder = this.db.getOrderByPubKeyNonce(pubKeyAx, nonce);
if (dbOrder && dbOrder.status !== "pending") {
  // Another instance already matched — skip
  continue;
}
```

Applied to both:
1. `onRemoteOrderArrived()` — before sending trade offer
2. `handleTradeOffer()` — before accepting trade offer

### Defense layers

| Layer | Scope | Prevents |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `lockingOrders` Set | Single instance | Intra-process double-match |
| **DB status check (new)** | **Multi-instance** | **Cross-instance double-match** |
| On-chain nullifier | Global | Double-settlement (ultimate guard) |

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `zk-relayer/src/core/cross-relayer-matcher.ts` | DB guard in both match paths |

Adds a new `src/01_matmul/` directory with an OpenACC port of the BLAS GEMM benchmark (`C = α·A·B + β·C`), supporting float and double precision.

## Key files

- **`main.cpp`** — OpenACC kernel using `#pragma acc parallel loop collapse(2)` with inner `reduction(+:s)`, wrapped in an `#pragma acc data` region; includes a host reference implementation for correctness validation and a timed benchmark loop
- **`utils.h`** — Shared helpers: `rand_matrix`, `performance` (GFLOP/s reporting), `print_2x2_matrix_values` (DEBUG only)
- **`Makefile`** — Auto-detects compiler: NVHPC (`nvc++ -acc=gpu -gpu=$(GPU_ARCH)`) or GCC (`-fopenacc`)

## Kernel structure

```cpp
#pragma acc parallel loop collapse(2) \
    present(A[0:M*K], B[0:K*N], C[0:M*N])
for (int i = 0; i < M; i++) {
  for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
    fp s = fp(0);
    #pragma acc loop reduction(+:s)
    for (int k = 0; k < K; k++)
      s += A[i * K + k] * B[k * N + j];
    C[i * N + j] = alpha * s + beta * C[i * N + j];
  }
}
```

## Build

```bash
# NVHPC
make CC=nvc++ GPU_ARCH=cc80

# GCC
make CC=g++

./main 1024 1024 1024 100
```

author: clubanderson
body:
Closes #6344

## Root cause

The deploy streak that started at 2026-04-11 08:16 UTC and persisted across 4 subsequent commits (`e05e6fb7`, `2c654e42`, `c1a0b426`, `a6d4b111`) was caused by the chart default `securityContext.runAsUser: 1001` that #6329 added to fix Kind/Minikube.

On `pok-prod` and `vllm-d`, the target clusters are OpenShift. OpenShift's `restricted` / `restricted-v2` SCC allocates a **namespace-specific UID range** (e.g. `1000710000-1000719999`) and rejects pods whose explicit `runAsUser` falls outside that range — **silently**, with no container-level error message. The helm upgrade just spins for 5 minutes and rolls back with `Replicas: 0/1 / context deadline exceeded`.

Last known-good deploy was `a2967b09` at 08:00 UTC, right before #6329 landed. Every push-to-main deploy after that failed with the identical pattern.

## Fix

Override the chart defaults in the two OpenShift `Deploy with Helm` steps:

```yaml
--set securityContext.runAsUser=null \
--set securityContext.runAsGroup=null \
--set securityContext.runAsNonRoot=null \
```

This unsets the values so SCC's pod mutation webhook can inject its own namespace-appropriate UID/GID. Kind/Minikube and other non-SCC clusters still get the `runAsUser: 1001` chart default untouched — nothing changes for them.

Also added a matching troubleshooting section to the chart README so OpenShift operators outside the CI workflow (#6344 will hit everyone running this on OpenShift, not just pok-prod/vllm-d) find the workaround.

## Test plan

- [x] `helm lint` passes
- [x] `.github/workflows/build-deploy.yml` parses as valid YAML
- [ ] Post-merge deploy to vllm-d succeeds
- [ ] Post-merge deploy to pok-prod succeeds

author: alies-dev
body:
## Issue to Solve

`view()` and `ResponseFactory::view()` were annotated with `@psalm-taint-sink html $data`, causing `TaintedHtml` for every controller that passes user input to a Blade view — even when the template safely uses `{{ $var }}`.

## Related

Closes #684

## Solution Description

Blade auto-escapes all `{{ $var }}` output via `htmlspecialchars()`. Real XSS requires `{!! $var !!}` (raw echo), which Psalm cannot detect since it doesn't parse `.blade.php` files. The html sink annotations created false positives with no detection benefit.

Removed `@psalm-taint-sink html` from all Blade view data parameters:
- `view()` helper — `$data`, `$mergeData`
- `Factory::make()`, `file()`, `first()`, `renderWhen()`, `renderUnless()`, `renderEach()`, `share()`
- `View::with()`
- `ResponseFactory::view()` — `$data`

File/include sinks on `Factory::file($path)` and html sinks on `ResponseFactory::make()`, `json()`, `jsonp()` are kept — those produce raw HTML responses.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests cover the change (3 new `Safe*` type tests replacing 16 false-positive tests)

body: ## Overview This PR is a complete rewrite of the OpenBlink VS Code extension, transforming it from a monolithic single-file architecture into a well-structured, modular codebase. The goal is to improve maintainability, testability, and extensibility for future development. This entire rewrite was developed with the assistance of [Windsurf](https://windsurf.com/) (Cascade AI), which contributed to code architecture design, implementation, documentation, and CI/CD configuration. ## Motivation The original `extension.ts` contained all logic in a single large file, making it difficult to: - Understand individual responsibilities - Test components in isolation - Add new board support or features - Onboard new contributors This rewrite addresses all of these concerns with a clean separation of concerns. ## Changes ### 1. Architecture Refactoring (`refactor!`) The monolithic `extension.ts` has been split into 7 focused modules: | Module | Responsibility | |--------|---------------| | `types.ts` | Shared types, enums, and interfaces | | `protocol.ts` | BLE protocol encoding/decoding with CRC8 checksum | | `ble-manager.ts` | BLE device scanning, connection management, and data transfer | | `board-manager.ts` | Board detection and configuration loading | | `compiler.ts` | mruby source → WASM bytecode compilation pipeline | | `ui-manager.ts` | VS Code webview panels, status bar, and user interactions | | `extension.ts` | Simplified entry point that wires all modules together | ### 2. Build System (`build`) - **Vendor submodules**: Added `emsdk` and `mruby` as git submodules under `vendor/` - **WASM build**: Added `mruby_build_config.rb` for Emscripten compilation (`MODULARIZE=1`, `ENVIRONMENT=node`, no `eval()`) - **Makefile**: Orchestrates the WASM build pipeline (setup → compile → copy) - **Webpack**: Updated with `copy-webpack-plugin` for resource bundling - **ESLint**: Migrated from `.mjs` to flat config format (`.js`) - **TypeScript**: Updated `tsconfig.json` compiler options ### 3. Board Configuration System (`feat`) Added a pluggable board configuration system under `resources/boards/`: - **`generic`**: Default board with comprehensive mruby API reference and sample program - **`m5stamps3`**: M5StampS3 support with localized reference docs (en/ja/zh-cn/zh-tw) - **`xiao-nrf54l15`**: Seeed XIAO nRF54L15 board support Each board directory contains: - `config.json` — board metadata (name, BLE service/characteristic UUIDs) - `reference.md` — API reference documentation (with optional localized variants) - `sample.rb` — starter mruby program ### 4. Internationalization (`feat`) - Added `@vscode/l10n` runtime bundle files for 4 locales: `en`, `ja`, `zh-cn`, `zh-tw` - Added `package.nls.*.json` for VS Code UI string localization (commands, menus, settings) ### 5. CI/CD Workflows (`ci`) Replaced the single monolithic `cicd.yml` with 3 focused workflows: | Workflow | Purpose | |----------|---------| | `ci.yml` | Lint and build checks on push/PR | | `release.yml` | Automated VSIX packaging and GitHub Release creation | | `wasm-build.yml` | mruby WASM compilation pipeline | ### 6. Documentation (`docs`) Added comprehensive project documentation under `doc/`: - `architecture.md` — Module overview with Mermaid diagrams - `ble-protocol.md` — BLE communication protocol specification - `board-configuration.md` — Board config file format and authoring guide - `build-system.md` — WASM build pipeline documentation - `compiler.md` — mruby compilation flow - `contributing.md` — Contribution guidelines - `i18n.md` — Internationalization guide README.md has been rewritten to reflect the new architecture. ### 7. Cleanup (`chore`) - Removed obsolete scaffolding: `.vscode-test.mjs`, `vsc-extension-quickstart.md`, `global.d.ts`, `types.d.ts`, `package_mod.js` - Removed outdated docs: `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.ja.md`, `README.zh-CN.md` - Removed unused VS Code config: `extensions.json`, `tasks.json` - Renamed `LICENSE.txt` → `LICENSE` - Reorganized WASM resources into `resources/wasm/` - Added new extension icon (`resources/icons/openblink.svg`) ## Testing - Added unit tests for the `protocol` module (`src/test/suite/protocol.test.ts`) ## Breaking Changes This is a complete architecture overhaul. The internal module structure has been redesigned from scratch. ## Commit History | Commit | Description | |--------|-------------| | `chore:` | Remove obsolete files and update project settings | | `build:` | Add vendor submodules, mruby build config, and tooling | | `refactor!:` | Modularize extension into separate modules | | `feat:` | Add board configurations and i18n localization | | `ci:` | Replace CI/CD workflows | | `docs:` | Add comprehensive project documentation | ## Note on AI Assistance All commits in this PR include `Co-authored-by: Windsurf Cascade ` to reflect that this work was developed collaboratively using Windsurf's Cascade AI agent for architecture design, code generation, documentation authoring, and CI/CD configuration. ---

body:
## Summary

This PR implements **Branch 5** of the Groww-native execution convergence plan.

It removes the remaining legacy direct LIVE execution path, makes runtime-backed execution the sole normal live model, and downgrades legacy recovery/reconciliation behavior to archival or historical support where still needed.

A follow-up blocker fix was also applied so post-write runtime notification failures no longer escape after a durable session/eligibility event has already been recorded.

---

## What changed

### Legacy LIVE execution path removed
- Removed the remaining legacy direct LIVE broker submission fallback from `ExecutionEngine`
- LIVE now fails closed unless a runtime-backed Groww path is available
- Direct broker placement is effectively paper-only

### Runtime-backed LIVE remains the sole normal path
Normal live execution model is now:

`eligibility -> session -> runtime -> runtime dispatch -> Groww broker -> runtime reconciliation`

### API state wiring updated
- `APIStateStore.register_execution_engine()` now binds LIVE engines to runtime-backed routing without any legacy fallback flag
- No normal or emergency legacy direct LIVE submit path remains in active operation

### Legacy recovery / reconciliation demoted
- Legacy broker recovery records are now treated as archival/observational only
- They no longer block normal runtime-backed live execution readiness or permission checks
- Legacy reconciliation inspect still rejects runtime-managed orders

### Blocker fix: notification failures no longer escape after durable write
In `api/state.py`:
- wrapped post-write runtime notification follow-ups in:
  - `record_session_event()`
  - `record_eligibility_event()`
- preserved durable-write-first ordering
- notification failures now emit warning logs instead of raising
- relevant IDs are included in the warnings

This prevents false 500-style failure behavior after a session/eligibility event has already been durably recorded.

---

  trading-bot/tests/test_live_execution_gate.py \

body:
Adds tactile feedback across the agent-facing hot paths and brings the inbox up to the same FlatList performance level the leads screen got in batch 3. Bumps app version to 1.2.0 so the rollout is visible in TestFlight / Play Console metadata.

Haptics infrastructure:
- `lib/haptics.ts` — thin wrapper around `expo-haptics` with three things the raw API doesn't give you: (1) no-op on web and on iOS simulators without a Taptic engine so screens don't have to branch on `Platform.OS`; (2) a 40ms debounce so back-to-back taps can't double-fire the engine within a frame; (3) semantic role names (`hapticTabSwitch`, `hapticRowTap`, `hapticButtonPress`, `hapticSuccess`, `hapticWarning`, `hapticError`, `hapticSelectionChange`, `hapticDestructive`) so if Apple ever changes the preferred impact-style mapping we fix it in one place. Android is intentionally silent for now — the Taptic fidelity there is rough enough that most apps leave row taps silent, and iOS is where the target users spend their day.

Wire-ups:
- `(tabs)/_layout.tsx` — `tabSwitch` tick on every tab press via `screenListeners.tabPress`.
- `(tabs)/leads.tsx` — `rowTap` in `handleRowPress`.
- `(tabs)/inbox.tsx` — `rowTap` in the new `handleRowPress` (also migrated to the memo'd row + stable renderItem pattern, see below).
- `(tabs)/calendar.tsx` — `rowTap` on all three row types (appointment, task, follow-up), `buttonPress` on New, `warning` + conditional `error` on `cancelEvent`, and `success` + conditional `error` on `completeTask`.
- `(tabs)/settings.tsx` — `selectionChange` + conditional `error` on every push-preference toggle, `warning` + conditional `error` on sign-out, `buttonPress` on the Notification center and Replay onboarding rows.
- `app/lead/[id].tsx` — `selectionChange` on pipeline stage pick, `success` + `error` on next-task completion, `warning` + `error` on next-appointment cancel.
- Three composer modals (`AppointmentComposerModal`, `BookingLinkComposerModal`, `TaskComposerModal`) — `success` haptic once the server persists the new record, `error` if the save fails.
- `EmailReplyModal` — `success` after the send promise resolves, `error` on throw.
- `LeadReplySection` SMS send — `success` once the SMS is actually on the wire (not pre-network), `error` on API failure. This is the highest-stakes action in the app so the feedback deliberately matches reality.

Inbox FlatList perf (matches what leads.tsx got in batch 3):
- Renamed `ThreadRow` → `ThreadRowInner`, wrapped in `memo`.
- `handleRowPress` is a stable `useCallback` so the memoized row can actually skip re-renders when the parent re-renders.
- `renderItem` and `keyExtractor` are both `useCallback`'d so they don't thrash the underlying FlatList.
